data.title: Simcere’s Xianlinda Approved for Marketing in China
data.description:
Simcere Pharmaceutical Group Limited ( (HK:2096) ) has shared an update.

Simcere Pharmaceutical Group said Xianlinda (Deunoxavir Marboxil Tablets), an anti-influenza drug developed through cooperation between a group subsidiary and Jiaxing AnDiCon Biotech, received approval from China’s National Medical Products Administration for marketing. The approval covers uncomplicated influenza A and B in previously healthy adolescents aged 12 and older and adults, excluding patients at high risk of influenza-related complications.

Xianlinda is described as an endonuclease inhibitor for influenza polymerase acidic protein; the release says research showed an absence of central nervous system side effects, oral absorption unaffected by food intake and a higher safety dose. The product is taken as one tablet, and the release says it can stop influenza-virus replication within 24 hours.

data.title: ShiFang Holding Discloses Chen Ye Funding-Support Proposal
data.description:
ShiFang Holding Limited ( (HK:1831) ) has provided an update.

ShiFang Holding disclosed that executive Director Chen Ye had submitted a funding-support proposal to its board. The proposal is conditional on protection of original shareholders’ rights and interests and includes his stated willingness to contribute at least RMB200 million in cash for sustainable operating funds, intended to help satisfy conditions for resuming trading.

Chen Ye also offered an additional HK$10 million and advances for specified creditor obligations and Chinese Mainland legal fees; major creditors, employees with wage arrears, and certain directors and former directors would cooperate through financial-support documents. If shareholder protection cannot be achieved, Chen Ye and other affected parties may pursue legal proceedings seeking a winding-up on insolvency; several directors supported the proposal, while Chen Zhi expressed no opinion, and matters involving Hu Bin and Wu Wenlin remain pending with Shenzhen police.

data.title: Bepirovirsen Approved in China as First-in-Class Functional Cure for CHB
data.description:
Sino Biopharmaceutical ( (HK:1177) ) has issued an announcement.

Sino Biopharmaceutical, a biopharmaceutical company, announced that China’s NMPA approved bepirovirsen (Hibsago) for marketing as a first-in-class functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. It is approved with nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy for non-cirrhotic adults who have received that therapy for at least six months, with HBV DNA below 90 IU/mL and HBsAg at or below 3,000 IU/mL.

Approval followed pooled B-Well phase III results: six-month treatment produced a 19% functional-cure rate, or 233 of 1,220 participants, versus zero of 614 receiving placebo. The rate was 26% in participants with HBsAg at or below 1,000 IU/mL, while Chinese subgroup rates ranged from 24% to 61% across HBsAg thresholds; reported adverse events included injection-site erythema, local pain and temporary liver-enzyme increases.

Chronic hepatitis B affects more than 240 million people globally, including approximately 75 million people in China, and contributed to an estimated 450,000 deaths in China in 2023. The release notes that many patients require lifelong antiviral therapy and that functional cure is associated with reduced risk of long-term complications, including liver cancer.
